quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash along the highway.
Workers are on or very close to the road ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very close to the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the roadway. Drive carefully through this work zone.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: At high speeds, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip, and your vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: Must you signal every time you pull away from a curb?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning so you can stay in control, stay in your lane, and respond to unexpected situations.

questions.question: Which lights should you use in bad weather or poor light conditions?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back and cause glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle hydroplanes, slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes. Braking can make hydroplaning worse.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before moving back. Always check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: If a driver feels worried, nervous, angry, or sad, what should they do?

options.text: They will drive normally without any problems.
They can drive faster because their senses are sharp.
They should calm down before starting the engine.
They should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should calm down before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, sadness, or excitement make it hard to focus on driving. Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to let other drivers know when you are turning.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen when someone drinks alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You are less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, blurs your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces alertness, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you calm down or focus.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medication and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if you take the recommended dose.
Any medicine prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines commonly cause drowsiness. Always check how your medicine affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that you must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see around you.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Turn your head to look through the rear window so you can see everything. Children and small objects are hard to see in mirrors. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend 200 feet directly behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet behind them. Do not follow closely behind large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There are more vehicles on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as clearly as during the day. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver can stop the vehicle.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver can stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle is approaching. You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. When an oncoming vehicle is near, slow down and let it pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
It tells you which cities and towns are ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws and rules.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They warn you about conditions on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is needed to react properly to things on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a problem.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you plan to enter or cross. Be ready to stop, but you can go if there is no traffic in the way.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Go around the pedestrians on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before you go.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and another vehicle?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles with trailers may not see you directly behind them. Keep extra distance from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road, so stay back to see around them.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane. Do not use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: When the road is wet, slow down.
The road ahead has a series of turns and curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet, slow down.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road is slippery when wet. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. As a driver, you are responsible for being aware of pedestrians and giving them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: It is more dangerous to drive at night than during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of low visibility and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating a hazard. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you too closely, release the accelerator. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn at an intersection, continue to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering and driving through a work zone. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle has the speed to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if you can see the road clearly ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle can reach the speed needed to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines mean any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
They brake slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you may not have time to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist stops suddenly.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, should you yield the right-of-way?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with disabilities who use a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device have the right-of-way whether on a sidewalk or road.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions and no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, what must you do?

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings, approach with extreme caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings and for multiple trains.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Your weight, biological sex, how much food you have eaten, and how much alcohol you have consumed all affect how your body absorbs alcohol. Only time removes alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows that the road has a sharp curve in the direction the arrow points. You may see several of these signs along a curve.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines also separate same-direction lanes but can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic.

questions.question: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle, increase your following distance to:

options.text: Three to four seconds.
Two seconds.
One second.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three to four seconds.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance to at least three to four seconds when following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle. Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers cannot see you if you are too close. They may slow down suddenly without knowing you are there.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Be alert for their presence and follow their directions at all times.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit or turn, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or place where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect light back at you in these conditions, creating glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: When you want to change lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while within an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while within an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:

options.text: Slowing down.
Merging into a different lane.
Maintaining your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging into a different lane.
questions.explanation: Help cars entering the freeway by moving to the next lane if possible. This creates a gap for them to enter safely. If you cannot merge, adjust your speed to help them merge smoothly.

questions.question: Which of the following about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
It is best to use snow tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and requires extra caution. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills to prevent skidding. Follow other vehicles at a greater distance than usual. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and its surroundings is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space around your vehicle so you have time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: Which of the following affect(s) how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: The amount of food in the stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All three choices
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while you drink slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.
